items.title: Test-retest reliability of spectral parameterization by 1/f characterization using SpecParam
items.authors: Daniel J. McKeown, Anna J. Finley, Nicholas J. Kelley, James F. Cavanagh, Hannah A. D. Keage, Oliver Baumann, Victor R. Schinazi, Ahmed A. Moustafa, and Douglas J. Angus
items.feature_family: Test-retest reliability of periodic and aperiodic spectral power features
items.feature_definition: SpecParam/FOOOF parameterization of EEG spectra into periodic peak parameters (power, central frequency, bandwidth) and aperiodic exponent/offset; repeated across resting eyes-open/eyes-closed and cognitive task recordings.
items.prediction_rationale: Inference: a feature family with measurable within-person test-retest stability provides a baseline for expected feature noise and repeatability; this is reliability evidence, not evidence that the feature detects pain or preserves amplitude under denoising.
items.verified_result_metric: Full-text qualitative result extracted: aperiodic exponent and offset were generally reliable; parameterized alpha/beta activity was more reliable than theta, with eyes-open fitting/data-loss limitations. Numeric metrics not copied into this record.
items.prediction_target: Test-retest reliability of EEG periodic/aperiodic spectral parameters; no pain prediction target.
items.validation_design: Secondary analysis of the publicly released 60-person repeated-session OpenNeuro cohort; the paper's analyzed sample was 49 healthy young adults across three sessions (two same-day sessions and a session about one month later), with rest and three cognitive tasks.
items.data_access_status: Public EEG recordings verified on OpenNeuro; article explicitly identifies the original 60-person dataset. The repository contains BIDS EEG files; this record does not claim the derived SpecParam features themselves are raw EEG.
items.data_evidence: The paper's Data availability section identifies OpenNeuro ds004148 as its original 60-person cohort. OpenNeuro landing page reports 64-channel, 500-Hz recordings and participant files; this is actual recorded EEG, separate from the paper's derived spectral parameters.
items.relevance_limitations: Healthy young adults and resting/cognitive states only; it evaluates spectral reliability, not pain, blink artifact removal, or the reliability of short 5-s C3/C4/Cz time-domain variance. Does not establish pain specificity.

items.title: Test-Retest Reliability of Single Spectral Power and Spectral Power Ratios in Relative and Absolute Values
items.feature_family: Absolute/relative band power and band-power ratios; test-retest ICC
items.feature_definition: FFT-derived absolute and relative single-band power and spectral power ratios computed across five scalp regions; alpha/beta ratio singled out for reliability comparison.
items.prediction_rationale: Inference: ratios may provide more repeatable strength features across sessions than absolute or relative single-band power, motivating reliability-first evaluation before clinical or pain prediction; not a denoising result.
items.verified_result_metric: Full text reports absolute alpha/beta ratios in central, parietal, occipital, and temporal regions with ICC > 0.75 in both datasets; the article reports the direction as more reliable than single-band absolute/relative power.
items.prediction_target: Short- and long-term reproducibility of EEG spectral-power features, not pain ratings or pain classification.
items.validation_design: Two independent healthy-adult datasets: Dataset 1, 60 people across three sessions (two same day, one month later); Dataset 2, 74 people with sessions one hour apart. Repeated-measures reliability assessed using ICCs. Dataset 1 overlaps the publicly released ds004148 cohort used by the SpecParam paper; Dataset 2 is an additional OpenNeuro cohort.
items.data_access_status: Public OpenNeuro EEG datasets verified by the paper's Data Availability Statement. ds004148 provides the repeated-state 60-person EEG cohort; ds003478 provides EEG records but its README notes some channel interpolation and that raw pre-interpolation data are unavailable, so not all data are pristine original acquisition files.
items.data_evidence: Full paper names OpenNeuro ds004148 and ds003478 in its Data Availability Statement. OpenNeuro pages expose participant-level EEG BIDS files. The ds003478 README explicitly notes that some channels were interpolated and there are no raw data to revert to; thus the dataset is public EEG but includes processing caveats.
items.relevance_limitations: Transferable repeatability evidence only: no pain labels, no pain-validation cohort, and no denoising intervention. Ratio-based spectral features differ from time-domain variance and may not transfer to low-density central-channel pain analyses. Dataset 1 overlaps a cohort in the SpecParam study; Dataset 2 adds a distinct repository/cohort.

items.title: Artifact-reference multivariate backward regression (ARMBR): a novel method for EEG blink artifact removal with minimal data requirements
items.authors: L. Alkhoury, G. Scanavini, S. Louviot, A. Radanovic, S. A. Shah, and N. J. Hill
items.feature_family: Blink-denoising reconstruction quality and signal-preservation metrics (SNR, RMSE, correlation, PSD and ERP preservation)
items.feature_definition: Regression of a simplified time-locked blink-reference signal against multichannel EEG, followed by artifact projection; evaluates semi-synthetic ground-truth reconstruction with RMSE/SNR/Pearson correlation, and real-data impacts using normalized correlation, PSD relative error, and preservation of event-related potentials.
items.prediction_rationale: Inference: denoising should be assessed not only by artifact reduction but also by preservation of EEG amplitude/spectral/event-related structure; better signal-quality metrics need not imply improved pain prediction.
items.verified_result_metric: Full text reports qualitatively lower RMSE and higher SNR/correlation than two MNE-native methods on semi-synthetic data; comparable or better performance to ASR/ICA+ICLabel in scenarios; real-data tests report ERP preservation. No numeric effects copied.
items.prediction_target: Blink-artifact suppression and preservation of EEG-derived signal/ERP features; explicitly not a pain target.
items.validation_design: Semi-synthetic blink-contaminated EEG benchmark constructed from real EEG (10 participants), plus real natural-speech EEG evaluation (16 participants analyzed) and an OpenNeuro visual-oddball ERP dataset (42 participants); article describes training/testing splits and supplementary online tests.
items.data_access_status: Public derived EEG verified: OSF exposes clean and blink-signal MAT files used for semi-synthetic validation. These are EEG-derived benchmark signals, not raw full-session EEG; public code is not counted as data. The paper additionally reports real EEG source corpora, but the linked OSF deposit inspected here is verified for semi-synthetic data only.
items.data_evidence: The paper states the semi-synthetic and real signals are available from its OSF/GitHub resources. OSF API file listings verify files including Sub1_Clean_EEG.mat and Sub1_Blink_Signal.mat under SemiSyntheticData. Those paired files are derived/semi-synthetic signal data. The article describes real natural-language and OpenNeuro ERP recordings separately; this record does not mislabel the OSF pair files as raw recordings.
items.relevance_limitations: Transferable denoising methods only; blink artifacts and 128-channel/event-related designs differ from pain experiments and resting 5-s windows. No pain ratings or pain-label performance. Semi-synthetic source-EEG benchmarks should not be interpreted as entirely raw independent recordings; linked validated pair files are transformed/derived.

conflicts.title: EEG denoising articles returned by targeted searches (including PhysioNet/BCI and dry-electrode candidates)
conflicts.status: Checked, not added without qualifying evidence
conflicts.reason: Search results included software/benchmark duplicates, recent methods without verified public raw EEG, or studies where a repository/full text was not independently checked in this limited pass. No such result is promoted based only on an abstract snippet.

gaps: The strict gap fill yielded 3 additional eligible original papers, not 30–40 and not 100. The highest-confidence additions are one open raw-data spectral-parameter reliability study, one cross-dataset band-power-ratio reliability study, and one open semi-synthetic blink-denoising study. Do not represent this as satisfying the requested 100-item overall target.

No newly verified study in this pass jointly validates denoising or EEG variance features against pain ratings using an open raw pain EEG dataset. The reliability studies are transferable methods evidence only, not pain validation.

ARMBR's linked OSF files are public transformed/semi-synthetic EEG-derived signal pairs, not public raw full-session EEG. The paper reports additional real-data sources, but the exact raw corpus URL was not verified in this pass.

Open public raw datasets and open text are not enough to establish feature transfer: the SpecParam and spectral-ratio papers measure spectral feature repeatability in healthy cohorts, while pain specificity, short-window C3/C4/Cz stability, and denoising-related preservation remain untested.

Targeted search returned candidates that failed data-access checks (open code without EEG, paywalled full text, no confirmed dataset link, or dataset/data-descriptor rather than an original signal analysis). These are recorded under conflicts and are not counted toward the qualifying items.
